clue.text: Reversing disease, hospital stops work, what's needed in charge concerned with hitting targets?

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so these pieces go inside the word for labour

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: a thing reversing runs backwards, so the illness that follows is read from its end

parts.note: pox is a general word for a disease
H is the abbreviation on hospital signs
'it' is the very thing wanted, as in 'that's it'
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A medical bulletin: a disease in retreat, a hospital halting work, and a note on what's needed from whoever is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's needed' is 'it' in the sense of the very thing wanted, as in 'that's it'. The disease looks like the subject of the bulletin but is just raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxophily is the love and practice of archery, so its adjective describes anything to do with shooting arrows at a mark.

clue.text: Furthermore, housing that is sucked up

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside, so the short Latin phrase goes within

parts.note: 'to add' introduces a further point, just as furthermore does
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: An addendum noting that something has been sucked up, perhaps by a vacuum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furthermore' is replaced by the two-word phrase that does the same job, and the Latin abbreviation sits after its first D.
explanation.definitionFit: To suck up to someone is to flatter them servilely, which is what a toady does.

clue.text: Diseased plants have these: box sadly perishes

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters before it come out in a damaged order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A gardener's lament: diseased plants carry these, so the box hedge is dying.
explanation.walkthrough: Box here looks like a hedging shrub, fitting the plant story, but it is only letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: X-bodies are inclusions seen in the cells of plants infected with certain viruses, a sign of the infection.

clue.text: Graceful poses survive in slight reaction?

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another goes inside it

parts.note: pique is the irritation of feeling slighted
to last is to survive or endure

explanation.surface: Do elegant postures hold up as a small response to something?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective, small; it is the noun, an insult, and pique is how one reacts to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastique is the art of graceful, statue-like posing and slow movement in dance.

clue.text: Hamper not fully repaired to improve flight for 24?

indicators.note: something not fully there is short of its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to hamper is to impede or hinder

explanation.surface: A hamper only partly mended so a bird can fly better.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is KESTREL. To imp a hawk's wing is to graft in new feathers to mend damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Falconers imp a hawk by splicing replacement feathers into broken ones, restoring its flight.

clue.text: Turn two non-water-soluble plant products mostly into something to freshen air

indicators.note: turning something around makes it face the other way, so it is read backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: resin and oil are both plant products that will not dissolve in water

explanation.surface: Convert some plant extracts into an air freshener.
explanation.walkthrough: RESIN plus OI, the second product missing its end, turned round gives IONISER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ioniser charges air molecules to clear dust and smells from a room, a type of air purifier.

clue.text: Jaundiced core of views held by fractious critic

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within it
fractious means unruly, so the letters behave badly and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so only the middle letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the central letter of views

explanation.surface: A bitter reviewer's sour outlook at the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaundiced' suggests a cynical critic, but here it is the medical sense, yellowed skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Icterus is the medical term for jaundice, so icteric means affected by that yellowing condition.

clue.text: Large local beetle to fly low over Arkansas-Washington canal feature

parts.note: aircraft buzz a place by flying low over it
AR is the postal code for Arkansas
the US capital is Washington DC
a lock raises and lowers boats on a canal

explanation.surface: A big beetle flies low over a canal in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' means dialect: buzzard-clock is a regional English name for the cockchafer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockchafer or similar large flying beetle is called buzzard-clock in English dialect, from its droning flight.

clue.text: Gulag's occupants meet brightening star ballerina from St Petersburg

indicators.note: the occupants of a camp are those inside it, so only the inner letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the letters between the first and last of the camp's name
a nova is a star that suddenly flares much brighter

explanation.surface: A grim image of prison-camp inmates encountering a star dancer from Russia's old capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Galina Ulanova, born in St Petersburg in 1910, was the prima ballerina of the Kirov and then the Bolshoi.

clue.text: Point of verbal joke about corporation

parts.note: a pun is a joke made with words
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, as is tum

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the point is of a pun told about a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a business, but it is the old humorous word for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctum is a dot or small spot, Latin for a point, used in anatomy and in old musical notation.

clue.text: Not the most outstanding work, viz. one Zero Mostel, losing heart, developed

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
losing one's heart means the central letters of the name are cut out

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
the actor's surname, to have its middle pair removed

explanation.surface: A not-quite-top production starring Zero Mostel, the comic actor, who seems to have lost his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' plays on sculpture standing out from its background: this is half relief, not the full kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Mezzo-rilievo is half relief, carving whose figures project about halfway from the surface, less than alto-rilievo.

clue.text: Fractious critic's circle, one among lowest class of celebs

indicators.note: to be among a group is to sit within it, so the small pieces go inside

parts.note: the Z-list is the jokey bottom rank of celebrity, below the A-list
O has the shape of a circle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered reviewer's social circle turns out to be one of the Z-list nobodies.
explanation.walkthrough: O and I sit inside Z-LIST to give ZOILIST; the 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoilus was a Greek grammarian notorious for nit-picking Homer, so a zoilist is a carping, ill-natured critic.

clue.text: Fleming who composed and rejected last letter, drinking half of strong coffee

indicators.note: a drinker takes something in, so the coffee part goes inside
something rejected is sent back, so the letter's name is read backwards

parts.note: zed is the British name for Z, the last letter

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, so its second four letters are dropped

parts.note: espresso is strong black coffee

explanation.surface: A composer from Flanders turns down a final letter while gulping half an espresso.
explanation.walkthrough: DEZ takes in ESPR after its D to make DES PREZ. 'Fleming' looks like a surname, but it means a native of Flanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Josquin des Prez was the great Franco-Flemish Renaissance composer of masses and motets.

clue.text: Scotland's vulgar traitor yielding lead to Queen

indicators.note: giving up the front position to another means the opening letter is swapped out

parts.note: Judas betrayed Jesus, so his name means any traitor
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A crude Scottish turncoat steps aside to let the monarch go first.
explanation.walkthrough: JUDAS loses its J to R, giving RUDAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudas is a Scots adjective for coarse or unmannerly, often used of a rough old woman.

clue.text: In South America, what part of tree without new ring provides wood there?

parts.note: que is Spanish for what, the language of most of South America

indicators.note: going without something means doing without it, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a branch is a limb of a tree
N is the abbreviation for new
O has the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: A botanical question about which bit of a tree, stripped of a fresh ring, yields timber in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to South America, so the definition is a wood from that continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Quebracho is an extremely hard South American timber tree, its name meaning axe-breaker in Spanish.

clue.text: Including short witticism, recalls double entendres

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so the joke goes inside

parts.note: to evoke is to call to mind

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine, punctuated by quick jokes, brings back memories of saucy double meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivoke is an old spelling of equivoque, a pun or phrase with two meanings, one usually risqué.

clue.text: Aged reed tea the writer brought into Hawaiian feast

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: brought into a place means taken inside it, so this piece goes within the feast

parts.note: a luau is a traditional Hawaiian party feast
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Old Hawaiian grass, tea and the clue's author are all carried into a beach feast.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the writer goes inside the feast; the tea stays in front. 'Aged' is part of the definition, marking the instrument as old.
explanation.definitionFit: The chalumeau was an early single-reed woodwind, the forerunner of the clarinet, so an old reed instrument.

clue.text: Sign for and transfer into little woman's custody

indicators.note: something in custody is held inside, so the transfer goes within the name

parts.note: Amy March is one of the four sisters in Little Women
to pass something is to transfer it

explanation.surface: A legal note about signing for a child who is being moved into a young girl's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign for' sounds like signing for a delivery, but it is the symbol standing for the word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampassy is a dialect variant of ampersand, the name of the symbol &.

clue.text: Virus remedied with gold in infusion of leaves

indicators.note: the precious metal goes in, sitting inside the shuffled word
something remedied has been put right, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A herbal cure: a virus treated with gold dissolved in a leaf tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remedied' fits the medical story, but it only signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Uva-ursi, Latin for bear's grape, is bearberry, whose leaves are steeped as a traditional urinary remedy.

clue.text: Since mentioned previously, cropped purple fruit

indicators.note: something cropped is cut short, so its final letter is removed

parts.note: 'as' can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
the said item is the one already mentioned

explanation.surface: Back-reference to an earlier note about some trimmed purple fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is a spelling of açaí, the small purple berry of an Amazonian palm sold as a health food.

clue.text: Colouring from tropical fruit mustn't save energy

indicators.note: save can mean except, so the phrase is taken except for that letter

parts.note: people who mustn't do something are not to do it
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Advice that a dye made from exotic fruit must not be wasteful of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save energy' reads as conservation advice; 'save' means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnotto, also annatto, is an orange-red food colouring from the seed pods of a tropical American tree.

clue.text: Tin cap removed from snout to use it in the country?

definitions.text: to use it in the country?

indicators.note: removing a cap takes off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
an animal's muzzle is its snout

explanation.surface: Someone prises a tin lid off a pig's nose to see how it fares on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the snout, and 'in the country' means rural dialect: to snuzzle is to root or nuzzle with the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuzzle is a dialect verb meaning to nuzzle or snuffle, which is what an animal does with its snout.

clue.text: Machines phased out for retiring Geiger, say

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the short word for in favour of is read backwards

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Hans Geiger, inventor of the radiation counter, is one bearer of the name

explanation.surface: Old instruments are withdrawn as a physicist with a famous counter retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Geiger' wants to be the counter, a machine, but it is the physicist's first name that is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, an orphan is a model its maker has discontinued, leaving owners without support or upgrades.

clue.text: Website automatically generated hit with internal page

indicators.note: internal means on the inside, so the single letter is placed within

parts.note: to slog a ball is to hit it hard
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A bot-made site gets a hit on one of its inner pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A splog, from spam blog, is a fake blog churned out by software to boost search rankings or carry adverts.

clue.text: Taking a risky journey? No good leaving Tube to regulate flow

indicators.note: letters leaving a word depart from it, so they are struck out

parts.note: to venture is to set out on a risky undertaking
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Planning a risky trip? Don't go by the London Underground, which is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' reads as the London Underground, but it is a plain pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A venturi is a pipe with a narrowed throat, used to measure or control the speed of a fluid.

clue.text: Tanager's wings pinned by unusually sleek bird of prey

indicators.note: something pinned is held fast within, so these letters sit inside the others
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an abnormal order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: wings are the two sides, so only the outside letters of the bird's name are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the songbird's name

explanation.surface: A small songbird's wings are pinned by a strangely glossy raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hovers over verges hunting mice, a common raptor.

clue.text: Very old French bother this country: it's all over for loser at Borodino

indicators.note: 'over' says the whole lot is turned back to front

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
zut is a French exclamation of annoyance, like 'bother!'
the setter writes from the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A grumpy old Frenchman declares the game is up for this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's all over' sounds like defeat, fitting the battle, but it tells you to turn the whole string round. Borodino was the bloody 1812 battle before Napoleon entered Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Kutuzov commanded the Russian army at Borodino in 1812 and withdrew afterwards, leaving Napoleon to take Moscow.

clue.text: The speaker's phone operating system deal which may investigate audibility problems

parts.note: the person speaking says my
to ring someone is to phone them
OS is the standard abbreviation for operating system
to cope is to deal with something

explanation.surface: Tech-talk about a phone, its operating system and a contract deal that might check why calls sound faint.
explanation.definitionFit: A myringoscope is an instrument for examining the eardrum, so a doctor might use it on hearing complaints.
